_about: Standing specifications for a shared page, in a form a check can read.
Root cause R2 in the ISZE agent error register (18-19 Sep 2026): instructions sit in rule
files scoped to one folder, so the session that repeats the mistake never loads them. This
file is the fix: one machine-readable list of the specifications already given, with a check
that compares a page against them and reports disagreement.
Every row cites where the specification comes from. Nothing here is invented. A row whose
check type is 'manual' means exactly that: the tool cannot decide it, so it prints the rule
and the evidence and leaves the judgement to a person.
_extend: Add a row to the 'specifications' array. Required keys: id, title, statement, source, check.
check.type is one of: numeric_vocabulary, basis_cooccurrence, phrase_guard, manual.
See 02_dashboards/_build/check_page_specifications.py for what each type does and why some
sentences can only be reported rather than failed.

specifications.title: The AdBlue (urea) filter interval is the sourced figure, per engine family
specifications.statement: The AdBlue filter is a filter cartridge, not the AdBlue tank. Its replacement interval is 200,000 km (124,000 miles) on the N-series NPR75 / 4HK1 engine and 80,000 km (50,000 miles) on the F-series 4HK1-TCH. A page that prints an AdBlue or urea filter interval must print one of those sourced figures for the right engine family. No D-Max / light-commercial AdBlue interval is sourced, so no figure may be shown for that class.
specifications.why_it_was_added: Register error E09 (Critical, raised 7 times): the old interval was still on the page months after Jerome specified it. Counter measure CM09: the per-market interval table is the authority and a page that prints a different figure is a build error.

source.quote: | AdBlue filter | **200,000** | km (124,000 mi) | R | Severe X |
| AdBlue filter (if equipped) | **200,000** | km (124,000 mi) | R | |
| AdBlue filter (4HK1-TCH) | **80,000** | km (50,000 mi) | R | Severe X |
block quoting section 2: N-series NPR75 / 4HK1 200,000 km; F-series 4HK1-TCH 80,000 km; D-Max / LCV not in the sources
urea_filter 0.2 for N-series and UREA_FILTER_F_SERIES for F-series - the derived rate follows the sourced interval

check.note_on_values: The allowed set is taken from the source rows above, in km. The miles figures are the same rows' second column. A page may state either unit.
check.note_on_false_positives: The subject must be the AdBlue or UREA FILTER, within 20 characters, and the measure must sit within 120 characters of it. An earlier version matched the bare word 'AdBlue' and then read an oil interval out of a neighbouring table cell on ISZE_Pricing_Proposal_v1.html - a false failure on a legitimate page. The filter word is what makes the row about the filter.
check.message: an AdBlue or urea filter interval is printed that is not one of the sourced figures (200,000 km / 124,000 mi N-series; 80,000 km / 50,000 mi F-series 4HK1-TCH). Replace it with the sourced figure for the engine family the page is about, or remove it.

specifications.title: ITUK runs its own service schedule and the two schedules are never averaged
specifications.statement: ITUK runs the service schedule agreed with that distributor: filters 1.25 visits a year, clutch and brake 0.5, on a 22,389-vehicle fleet, with its own brake and shoe factor of 0.4. Every other market runs the internal schedule: standard trucks 0.5 visits a year, heavy 0.667, light vehicles 1.0. A page must not present one blended cover figure across both, and must not apply the ITUK basis to a non-ITUK market or the internal basis to ITUK.
specifications.why_it_was_added: Register error E09 and the recurring ITUK lane confusion. A blended ITUK figure is the single most dangerous cell the workspace has produced: one number carrying two systems. The register's own rejected-recycle list records this class.

source.quote: Two interval lanes, never averaged. ITUK runs the service schedule agreed with the distributor for that market: filters 1.25 visits a year, clutch and brake 0.5, on a 22,389-vehicle fleet, with its own brake and shoe factor of 0.4.
Every other market runs the internal schedule: standard CV 0.5 visits a year
ITUK oil-filter cover presented with a mixed numerator and denominator ... Never one tile with both.

must_not_contain.message: an ITUK figure appears to be averaged or combined with the rest of the network. ITUK runs its own schedule; report the two separately.
an ITUK figure appears to be averaged or combined with the rest of the network. Report the two lanes separately.

check.manual_review: Deciding whether a given cover percentage was computed on the ITUK basis or the internal basis needs the number's derivation, which the text does not carry. Print this rule beside the finding and check the figure against its source.
check.message: the two ITUK service schedules appear to be blended.

specifications.title: The 4-6% band is on the weighted base-price index, not on billed euro
specifications.statement: The 4-6% revision band binds on the weighted base-price index, defined as sum(billed quantity x prior base price) over the rows that carry a price on both sides. It is not a 4-6% move in billed euro and not a 4-6% move in the price list as a whole. A page that states or measures against a 4-6% band must state that basis.
specifications.why_it_was_added: The band was quoted repeatedly without its basis, and the pricing method had to be corrected twice on 18-19 September (register errors E03 and E05). The method itself is now settled as a price ratio read from the price list and must not be re-opened.

source.quote: The index the 4-6% binds on is `sum(billed quantity x prior base price)` over the rows that carry a price on both sides. [C] on `qty x prior_base_jpy` from `pricing_aim_source_lines.parquet`
Japan at +5.74% is inside the 4-6% band. Thailand at -2.45% is a price reduction
The 5.9616% is a YEN base-price move. The euro move is smaller because the net rate drift is -0.45% ... +5.48% in euro, which is already inside the 4-6% band.

check.forbidden_message: the 4-6% band is described as a move in billed euro. The band is on the weighted base-price index, not on billed euro.
check.message: the page states or measures against a 4-6% band without naming the basis it binds on (weighted base-price index, sum of billed quantity x prior base price). Add the basis, or the band reads as a move in billed euro.

specifications.title: A pickup is not a truck
specifications.statement: The D-Max is a pickup and runs the D-Max maintenance schedule. The N-series and F-series are trucks and run the N-series and F-series schedules. A page must describe each vehicle by its own body type: calling a pickup a truck is wrong on the product, and applying the truck schedule to a pickup is wrong on the arithmetic.
specifications.why_it_was_added: Register error E10 (High, raised 13 times): a pickup described as a truck on a handed-over page. Jerome, 19 Sep 06:28: 'why do you mention truck it's a pickup?'

source.quote: The N-series schedule for trucks, the D-Max schedule for pickups, weighted by this market's measured vehicles-in-service split.
Error register row E10: 'a pickup described as a truck'
band 'LCV_D-Max' is separate from '3.5t_N35', i.e. the pickup is its own class

must_not_contain.message: a pickup is described as a truck.
a truck is described as, or equated with, a pickup.

check.manual_review: The phrase guard only catches the direct equation. A page that uses the bare word 'truck' where it means a pickup, or applies the N-series schedule to D-Max fleet, will not be caught by a text match. check_rendered_page.py reports every page where 'truck' appears without the page naming a pickup, for a human read.
check.message: a pickup appears to be described as a truck.

specifications.title: A model code to tonnage band mapping must come from the sourced table, not a regex dictionary
specifications.statement: The tonnage band for a model code comes from the one authored map 03_analytics/Isuzu/prism/data/series_to_band.csv, read through modules/vehicle_bands.py (model_code_to_tonnage.csv is a table built from it by build_model_code_to_tonnage.py). A code the sources do not name must be left with an empty band. The numeric suffix (75 / 85 / 87 / 88 / 90) is a generation code, not a weight. In particular NMR88 is a 5.5-tonne truck (the European N55, ruled 2026-09-23) and must never be read as a 3.5-tonne N35.
specifications.why_it_was_added: Register error E13 (High, raised 28 times): the tonnage band rested on SERIES_TO_GVW in parse_epc_results.py, a regex dictionary with no source, so Malta and Cyprus both sat on NMR88 read as a 3.5-tonne truck. Counter measure CM08: the model-code to tonnage band comes from a sourced table with its own metadata.

source.quote: sources: Duncan Young / ITUK PMS brake deck slide 14; Rene Paul / GIDSS GIDSS_maint_{N,F}_MY{14,24}.pdf; JP VIN register series -> GVW map; epc_decode_batch1; genuine_bvp_crossref

rules: 'The numeric suffix (75 / 85 / 87 / 88 / 90) is a generation code, not a weight ... NLR appears as 85, 87 and 88 and all three are 3.5 t ... FRR90 and FSR90 share the suffix 90 at 11 t and 13.5 t.'
rules: 'A code the sources do not name is left with an empty band and confidence=unresolved. An unresolved code is a better answer than a plausible one.'
Error register row E13: 'Malta and Cyprus were both sitting on NMR88 read as a 3.5-tonne truck'

must_not_contain.message: NMR88 is being read as a 3.5-tonne N35. NMR88 is a 5.5-tonne truck (European N55); the 88 is a generation code, not a weight.
NMR88 is being read as a 3.5-tonne N35. NMR88 is a 5.5-tonne truck (European N55).

check.manual_review: This guard catches the named defect only. Whether every band on a page came from the sourced table needs the page's own provenance line; the check cannot see it. Confirm the page's footer names model_code_to_tonnage.csv and that its unresolved codes are excluded rather than guessed.
check.message: an unsourced tonnage band appears on the page.
